acceptance.assertion: Measure current snapshot size and project repository, clone and checkout growth across realistic Commonworld release cadences; define explicit thresholds or a bounded horizon rather than relying on an unbounded append-only assumption.

Compare at least bounded in-Git retention with external immutable deployment-artifact storage (or an equivalent architecture), including GitHub Pages compatibility, current-release selection, exact readback, operational complexity and rollback consequences.

Any pruning, compaction or migration is prohibited from deleting the shared common-ancestor release tree during ordinary independent feature-branch builds. A deterministic concurrent-branch fixture proves that the T040 rename/delete conflict class remains absent and semantic source conflicts still fail closed.

The chosen lifecycle documents and validates the retained rollback/readback horizon, including how current release metadata and historical artifacts are restored together without shared-history rewrite or manual hash-directory selection.

Focused retention tests, deterministic build, full make validate, browser smoke, diff-bound self-review and required GitHub checks pass on the exact proposed head; closeout reports before/after storage growth and any remaining availability trade-off.

approval.note: Any retention or compaction mechanism must preserve T040 conflict resistance and must not delete the common-ancestor release tree as an ordinary feature-branch build side effect.

goal: Bound the repository and clone-size growth introduced by append-only immutable Commonworld release snapshots without reintroducing the generated rename/delete conflict class, weakening exact current-release readback, or losing the intended rollback horizon.

does_not_establish: that 5.03 MB is the long-term average release delta after Git compression
that every historical release must remain in Git indefinitely
permission to prune release artifacts from independent feature branches
permission to weaken exact readback or rollback guarantees

rollback.strategy: If a bounded-retention or external-artifact design weakens exact release readback, rollback integrity, GitHub Pages compatibility or T040 conflict resistance, revert the lifecycle changes together and retain append-only history while a safer design is developed.

title: Bound immutable release-history growth safely
